title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Communications & Templates
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard incident process, runbooks, postmortem template, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and customer/status-page communications templates. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, incident commanders, and product owners to follow during operational events.

Scope
- Applies to incidents affecting production-hosted Redwood API, Dedicated runtime endpoints, and Redwood Console core services.
- Includes severity definitions, escalation paths, runbook actions for common failure modes, communications templates, and postmortem expectations.

Key definitions and roles
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates the response, decisions, and post-incident write-up.
- SRE Lead: technical owner responsible for coordinating mitigations and runbook steps.
- Service Owner: product or engineering owner of the impacted service.
- Communicator: owns external/internal updates (status page, Slack, PagerDuty).
- On-call Engineer (Primary/Secondary): performs diagnostics, remediation, and hands off to follow-up owners.

Severity levels (use these for routing and SLAs)
1) P0 (Sev 0) — Critical outage
   - Symptoms: Platform-wide outage (all customers) or loss of control plane, data loss, or security incident.
   - Targets: Notify within 1 minute, IC engaged within 5 minutes, status page published within 15 minutes.
2) P1 — Major degradation
   - Symptoms: High error rates (>5% 5xx across traffic), sustained latency >2x SLO for >5 minutes for customer-facing endpoints, or partial data loss for a subset of customers.
   - Targets: Acknowledge within 5 minutes, IC engaged within 15 minutes, status page published within 30 minutes.
3) P2 — Minor degradation
   - Symptoms: Single-service errors affecting a small subset of traffic or degraded non-critical features.
   - Targets: Acknowledge in 1 hour, documented in incident tracker; may not require immediate status update.

Escalation matrix & timeouts
- Primary on-call: 0–5 minutes to respond.
- Secondary on-call: engaged at 10 minutes if primary unavailable or needs assistance.
- IC escalates to SRE Lead at 20 minutes for unresolved P0/P1.
- PagerDuty escalation policy MUST reflect these timeouts; maintain up-to-date phone/pager numbers in the on-call schedule.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
1) Detection & Triage
   - Verify alert source and severity. Check monitoring dashboards (Datadog), logs (ELK), and tracing (Jaeger).
   - If false positive, close alert with notes. If valid, create an incident in our incident tracker (Jira incident project) and assign an incident ID (INC-YYYY-XXXX).
2) Mobilize & Assign Roles
   - Assign IC, SRE Lead, Communicator, Service Owner. Document roles in the incident ticket.
3) Initial Actions (containment)
   - Execute relevant runbook (see Runbooks section).
   - If rolling back or failover is required, communicate planned action and expected impact on status page.
4) Mitigation & Recovery
   - Implement fixes, monitor metrics to confirm recovery.
5) Resolution & Closure
   - Once service is stable and SLOs are restored, update incident ticket with timeline and initial summary.
   - Publish resolution notice on status page and send customer summary if impacted.
6) Postmortem & Follow-up
   - IC or SRE Lead opens a postmortem within 48 hours. Postmortem must be published to Confluence within 7 business days with action items, owners, and due dates.

Runbooks (common playbooks and quick commands)
- Note: Runbook steps are prescriptive for immediate containment. If unfamiliar, escalate to SRE Lead. Always record every step in the incident ticket.

1) High 5xx rate on Redwood API (typical P1)
   - Verify: Datadog alert: api.*.5xx_rate > 5% for 5m.
   - Quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n redwood-api` ; `kubectl logs -n redwood-api <pod> --tail=200` ; check load balancer (ALB) 5xx metrics.
   - Mitigation options (in order):
     1. Remove suspect version from load balancer (traffic split rollback).
     2. Scale up replicas: `kubectl scale deploy redwood-api --replicas=<current+2> -n redwood-api` (temporary).
     3. Clear cache if CPU-bound: `redis-cli -h <host> FLUSHDB` only with owner approval.
     4. If root cause is model-serving runtime OOMs, failover to compatible model variant with less memory via routing policy.
   - Post-action: Monitor 5xx rate and latency for 15 minutes before declaring recovery.

2) Elevated latency for embeddings endpoint (P1/P2)
   - Verify: percentiles (P95/P99) on Datadog, check GPU utilization on fleet dashboard.
   - Mitigation: enable autoscale burst pool, route traffic to Dedicated nodes or lower-precision quantized model, temporarily throttle non-critical background jobs.

3) GPU node eviction or driver crash (P1)
   - Verify: node status in cluster, check node-exporter and nvidia-smi metrics.
   - Mitigation: cordon + drain: `kubectl cordon <node>` ; `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` ; restart inference pods on healthy nodes. Activate node replacement playbook in infra runbooks.

Diagnostic checklist (record each step)
- Timestamped actions, who ran them, commands used, and outputs (attach logs).
- Alerts consulted and dashboards/screenshots attached.
- Communications posted (Slack channel, status page links).

Rotations & on-call rules
- Rotation length: standard 1-week primary rotations, with secondary on-call assigned as backup.
- Handoffs: written handoff message in #oncall-ops Slack at shift start, include ongoing incidents and follow-ups.
- Time-off swaps: use the on-call scheduling tool (Opsgenie/PagerDuty) and notify team 72 hours in advance.
- Coverage hours: Primary expected to be available 24/7 while on shift; reasonable response times per severity above.
- Long-term on-call sickness or absence: engineering manager escalates to roster owner to find replacement.

Game days
- Frequency: quarterly platform game days + targeted runbook validation after major changes.
- Goals: exercise failover, validate runbooks, verify alert fidelity, and measure time-to-detect/mitigate.
- Typical scenarios: simulate ALB failure, model-serving node OOM spike, external dependency latency, and database replica lag.
- After-action: collect metrics, update runbooks within 5 business days, and publish a short recap to Confluence.

Postmortem template & expectations
- Timeline: Open postmortem within 48 hours; publish draft within 7 business days; finalize when action items have owners and dates.
- Required sections (use this as checklist):
  1. Title & incident ID
  2. Severity and services impacted
  3. Summary (1–3 sentence customer-facing description)
  4. Timeline (minute-granular events from detection to resolution)
  5. Root cause analysis
  6. Contributing factors
  7. Detection & mitigation notes (what worked/failed)
  8. Action items (owner, due date, status)
  9. Follow-up plans and verification steps

Status page & customer communications templates
- Principles: Be timely, transparent, and avoid speculation. Use plain language for customers, technical details in internal updates.

1) Initial public status page entry (P0/P1) — short:
- Title: [Investigating] Increased error rates for Redwood API (INC-XXXX)
- Body: We are investigating elevated error rates affecting text generation requests. Some customers may experience timeouts or 5xx errors. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We will post updates every 30 minutes or as the situation changes.
- Impact: Partial outage for text generation API endpoints for some customers.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner.

2) Internal/partner update (Slack/email) — 1st update
- Subject: [INC-XXXX] Elevated 5xx on API — initial findings
- Body: Initial triage indicates a new model deployment increased memory pressure on inference runtime, causing retries and 5xx responses. Primary mitigations in progress: rolling back model variant and scaling inference pods. Expected impact: reduced errors within 15 minutes.

3) Customer-facing update (after mitigation underway)
- Subject: Update: We are seeing improvements to Redwood API errors
- Body: We have identified a deployment-related issue and are rolling back the change. Error rates are decreasing; some customers may still see intermittent errors. We will confirm full recovery within 30 minutes.

4) Resolution notice (public)
- Title: Resolved — Elevated error rates affecting Redwood API
- Body: The incident impacting text generation endpoints has been resolved. Root cause: a model deployment that increased memory pressure on inference nodes and caused retries leading to 5xx. Mitigation: rollback of the model, scaling of inference pods, and routing to a compatible model variant. We are conducting a postmortem and will publish action items within 7 business days.

Customer post-incident summary (template)
- Short summary of impact (time window, affected services)
- What we did to resolve it
- What we're doing to prevent recurrence (planned action items and ETA)

Communications process checklist
- IC confirms severity and approves public statement.
- Communicator posts to status.redwood.ai and notifies customers with open support tickets.
- Product and account teams send tailored notes to key customers if they had elevated impact.

Runbook & doc maintenance
- Owners must review runbooks quarterly and after every postmortem.
- Action items that change runbooks must include a verification step and be signed off by SRE Lead.

Appendix — quick command references
- Get pods: `kubectl get pods -A -l app=redwood`
- Tail logs: `kubectl logs -n <ns> <pod> -c <container> --follow`
- Scale deployment: `kubectl scale deploy <name> --replicas=<n> -n <ns>`
- Restart service (systemd): `sudo systemctl restart <service>`

Contacts & escalation references
- On-call schedule: https://pagerduty.example.com/schedules/redwood-oncall
- Incident tracker: https://jira.example.com/projects/INCIDENTS
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai

Revision history
- 2025-11-10 — Created by Maya Thompson (initial playbook).
- 2026-02-15 — Updated escalation timeouts, added communications templates, and clarified runbook steps (reviewers: Diego Martinez, Hannah Lee, Omar Khan).
